messages:
emi: Urgent — multiple customers reporting sudden 5xx bursts on hosted inference endpoints, starting ~09:12 UTC. Major impact for two enterprise customers (billing spikes on usage dashboards). Opening thread to track.
ajay: Thanks, Emi. Any specific endpoints or models called out?
support-bot: Incoming customer report summary: customer_id=acme-corp, endpoints: /v1/generate (gpt-2-small), observed 500s and 502s, first seen 09:10 UTC, error rate ~18% for the last 10m. Billing spike noted for same window.
emi: ACME also attached a repro curl they used.
sophie: Can you paste the curl and the error body? Might help narrow auth vs model failures.
emi: Paste: ```curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data '{"model":"gpt-2-small","input":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -i``` Response snippet: ```HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
content-type: application/json
{"error":{"code":"gateway_timeout","message":"upstream error: model-service timeout (t=1500ms)"}}```
terry: 502 with upstream model-service timeout. Can we check model-serving pool logs? Maybe canary nodes overloaded.
ajay: Quick check: around 09:08 we started a staged rollout of feature-flag `enable_new_auth_flow` at 10%. Deploy bot shows: "deploy-bot: rollout start flag=enable_new_auth_flow target=10% by=ajay" — but I recall an ops script that accidentally used PERCENT=100 for a related env var during the job.
ops-bot: automated alert: config-push detected env var `NEW_AUTH_PERCENT=50` changed in k8s/hosts cluster-3 at 09:07 by ci/cd-job-2789.
maria: Wait — the flag system uses `enable_new_auth_flow` for routing to the new auth middleware, but the request router uses `NEW_AUTH_PERCENT` env var for percent-assisted routing. If those are out of sync, we could accidentally route more traffic than intended to the new path.
ajay: That would explain a sudden jump. The new path includes an additional token validation against billing-service to validate metered keys. If billing-service is slower under load it could add latency and cause upstream timeouts -> 502/504.
sophie: Can someone grab a sample trace? I see an increase in p50->p95 latency from 120ms to 800ms for the auth middleware in the last 10m.
emi: Attaching logs (sanitized): ```[09:10:23] router: incoming request id=xyz auth_route=NEW path=/v1/generate
[09:10:23] auth-new: validate token for key=k_***** latency=670ms status=200
[09:10:24] model-proxy: dispatch request id=xyz timeout=1500ms upstream=timeout error=upstream_timeout
[09:10:24] router: responded 502 to client id=xyz``` 
terry: Looks like token validation sometimes ok but adds latency; combined with model-proxy queueing -> timeouts.
maria: Billing spikes could be because the new auth path also performs an extra billing-usage fetch for every request to check quota. We added a cache with 60s TTL but it wasn't enabled for this canary config.
ajay: Confirmed — the canary config omitted `billing_cache_enabled=true` due to a missing template variable in the rollout manifest. So every canary request did a synchronous billing lookup.
emi: That's the root cause then: misconfigured canary (auth+billing sync lookup) got routed to much more traffic than intended because of env var mismatch, resulting in auth latency + billing lookup -> model upstream timeouts -> 5xx burst and inflated usage/billing counts.
support-bot: Customer messages: "we're seeing huge 500s and our daily bill spiked unexpectedly, please help ASAP" — ACME is on a support SLA.
ajay: Action plan: 1) Stop routing to new auth path (set NEW_AUTH_PERCENT=0) 2) Re-enable billing cache for canary or rollback flag entirely 3) Emergency metrics + reconcile billing spikes 4) Postmortem and rollout gating fixes.
terry: I'll take #1. Patching k8s env on router service now: `kubectl set env deploy/router NEW_AUTH_PERCENT=0 --namespace=prod --record` — running.
deploy-bot: rollout update: deployment/router env updated NEW_AUTH_PERCENT=0 by terry at 09:18 UTC. New replica configs being rolled.
ops-bot: healthcheck: router p95 latency returning to baseline within 90s. 5xx rate dropping from 18% -> 2%.
emi: Confirm with ACME and support team — pinged them that we're rolling back routing and investigating billing changes.
sophie: For #2, we should fix the canary manifest to include `billing_cache_enabled=true` and re-run the canary at a low percent with proper observability. Also add circuit-breaker on billing-service calls (short-circuit to cached results or soft-fail) so auth path doesn't cascade.
ajay: I'm going to trigger an immediate rollback for the `enable_new_auth_flow` flag via flags UI to be safe.
deploy-bot: feature-flag change: enable_new_auth_flow=OFF by ajay at 09:20 UTC (reason: emergency rollback)
support-bot: Notifying account team: @maria please keep ACME updated. Also create billing reconciliation ticket with finance.
maria: Notified ACME, told them the rollback is in progress and we'll provide a postmortem/credit if we find overbilling caused by our rollout.
emi: Repro steps for SRE/Eng: 1) Use the customer's API key, run 100 concurrent small generate requests at normal QPS 2) Observe 5xx rate and header path via router logs 3) Check billing-service latency and misses. Example load command: ````hey -n 100 -c 10 -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" -m POST -T application/json -d '{"model":"gpt-2-small","input":"x"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate```
terry: I'll run a controlled load against staging (with billing-service stubbed) to validate fix before re-roll.
ajay: Postmortem quick notes: root cause = mismatched canary config + missing caching flag -> synchronous billing lookups under canary + increased routing percentage caused by env var leak. Contributing: no circuit-breaker on billing lookup; rollout system didn't validate template variables; lack of secondary SLO gate (billing ops). Remediation already: rollback routing and flag.
emi: Next ops steps: - Create hotfix to add defensive default `billing_cache_enabled=true` in template - Add canary validation that compares flag state and router env var parity before rollouts - Add rate-limiter/circuit on billing-service calls - Finance: compute suspected overcharged tokens for ACME and propose credit.
maria: I've opened ticket FIN-1452 to reconcile usage and apply credit if needed. Also CC'd account manager.
ajay: I'll schedule a short postmortem for 2pm and invite Eng, SRE, Product, Finance.
support-bot: Customer ACME replied: "Thanks for the quick rollback. We'll wait for your postmortem and credits." :thumbsup:
emi: Closing live escalation — monitoring alerts still active but error rates are back down. Marking thread status: resolved (for now). We'll follow up in postmortem with timeline and concrete changes.
sophie: Also: temporary mitigation idea — make the billing lookup async and allow model-proxy to proceed with a soft quota warning to avoid hard timeouts in the future.
ajay: Agreed. We'll add to remediation backlog.
emi: Thanks everyone, great response. I'll collect logs and draft the incident timeline for the PM.
